title: The nftables in Istio's images is no longer pinned to 1.1.1 — nodes with an old nftables package can crash once a newer nft has run on them

detection.reason: the istio-cni ConfigMap's values and the nodes' package versions are not collected; the hint names the istio-cni DaemonSet and the command reads the nftables switch

quote: As a result, Istio is removing the `nftables` version pinning. Users are advised to update the `nftables` package on their nodes to the latest available version to ensure that the fixed version is installed. If you continue to experience `nftables` crashes on your nodes, downgrade to an older version of Istio and contact your node OS provider to request that the fix be backported to your OS version.
remediation: Only clusters that opted into native nftables (`global.nativeNftables=true`, rendered as `NATIVE_NFTABLES` in the istio-cni ConfigMap) are affected; iptables mode does not run nft. Before upgrading, update the `nftables` package on every node to a build carrying the upstream fix; a node whose nft crashes after the upgrade needs the fix from the OS vendor or a downgrade of Istio.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -n istio-system -l app=istio-cni -o json | jq -r '.items[].data.NATIVE_NFTABLES // "unset"'  # "true" means native nftables is on and every node's nftables package must carry the fix before 1.31

title: istiod 1.31 ignores a TCPRoute CRD below Gateway API bundle v1.6.0 — TCPRoutes stop being programmed

detection.reason: the bundle version is an annotation VALUE on the CRD and rules compare keys, not values; the hint names the TCPRoute CRD and the command prints its bundle version

quote: Resources backed by such CRDs are silently filtered by istiod, which previously made TLS passthrough breakage after upgrading to Istio 1.30 with stale Gateway API CRDs hard to discover.
remediation: istiod 1.31 watches TCPRoute at `v1` and drops a `tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io` CRD whose `gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version` annotation is below v1.6.0: no TCPRoute is read, the Gateway reports `attachedRoutes: 0` for its TCP listeners and that traffic fails with no error in the route's status. Upgrade the TCPRoute CRD to at least bundle v1.6.0 before upgrading istiod; `istioctl analyze` reports a stale CRD as IST0176. (The other gated CRDs are not new at 1.31: GRPCRoute v1.1.0 and BackendTLSPolicy v1.4.0 already applied, and TLSRoute v1.5.0 is the 1.30 rule.)
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o custom-columns='CRD:.metadata.name,BUNDLE:.metadata.annotations.gateway\.networking\.k8s\.io/bundle-version' --ignore-not-found  # below v1.6.0 is ignored by istiod 1.31

title: istiod now sends unhealthy endpoints to proxies unless a DestinationRule sets `outlierDetection.minHealthPercent`

detection.reason: applies to services WITHOUT minHealthPercent, an absence the projection cannot list; the istiod Deployment carrying the opt-out is the subject

quote: By default, Istio will now send unhealthy endpoints unless `OutlierDetection.minHealthPercent` is being configured on a Service. This can be disabled by setting `PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS` to `false` or using compatibility profiles.
remediation: For every service where no DestinationRule sets `outlierDetection.minHealthPercent` above 0, istiod now also sends the not-ready endpoints (marked unhealthy) and pins Envoy's panic threshold to 0 unless the DestinationRule sets one. Requests still go to ready pods only. What changes is locality-aware routing: not-ready pods now count against their zone's health, so with DestinationRule locality load balancing (`localityLbSetting` with outlier detection) traffic spills to other zones once under about 71% of a zone's pods are ready (Envoy's overprovisioning factor 1.4), where 1.30, which left not-ready pods out, kept it local while any ready pod remained; services using `trafficDistribution` already behaved this way. Check services that rely on zone-local traffic, or set `PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS=false` on istiod to keep the 1.30 behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS|PILOT_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # no printed line means unhealthy endpoints are sent after upgrade

title: Auto-registered WorkloadEntries created before the fix (1.29.6 / 1.30.3 / 1.31.0) stay on plaintext until re-registered or labelled `networking.istio.io/tunnel=http`

detection.reason: the affected entries are auto-registered AND missing the tunnel label — two conditions on one object the vocabulary cannot combine; the auto-registered entries are the candidates

quote: workloads auto-registered before upgrading continue to be reached over plaintext until either they re-register (reconnect a fresh instance) or the label (`networking.istio.io/tunnel=http`) is added to their existing WorkloadEntry.
remediation: Only meshes where VM proxies speak HBONE are affected: ambient-enrolled VMs, or sidecar meshes running with `ENABLE_HBONE=true` on the proxy and `PILOT_ENABLE_SIDECAR_HBONE_LISTENING=true` on istiod. There, for each auto-registered WorkloadEntry (annotated `istio.io/autoRegistrationGroup`) without the `networking.istio.io/tunnel` label, restart the VM/proxy so it re-registers, or add the label by hand — until then that workload is reached over plaintext. A plain sidecar mesh's unlabelled entries are correct as they are.
verifyCommand: kubectl get workloadentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations["istio.io/autoRegistrationGroup"] != null) | select(.metadata.labels["networking.istio.io/tunnel"] == null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each printed WorkloadEntry was auto-registered before 1.31 and stays plaintext until it re-registers or is labelled

title: `PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY` is removed — gateways always spawn an upstream span

detection.reason: checked on the istiod Deployment's container env NAMES only — a flag set through `pilot.env` in a values file lands there; one set via `meshConfig` or an IstioOperator that has not been applied yet is not scanned

quote: The environment variable `PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY` has been removed. The behavior it controlled (spawning a separate tracing span for each upstream request for gateway when using the Telemetry API) is now always enabled.
remediation: Remove the variable from istiod. If it was `false`, gateway traces gain one extra span per upstream request at 1.31; adjust trace-volume budgets or sampling accordingly. `compatibilityVersion: 1.30` lists the flag but it is inert there too.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # a printed line is the removed flag; a value of false means gateway traces gain an upstream span at 1.31

title: Large ambient meshes: ztunnel's reconnect request can exceed istiod's 4MiB gRPC limit and loop with `ResourceExhausted`

detection.reason: the trigger is the mesh's workload count, which the evaluator does not sum; the ztunnel DaemonSet marks an ambient mesh

quote: This request can exceed istiod's default 4MiB gRPC receive limit, leaving ztunnel in a reconnect loop with `ResourceExhausted: grpc: received message larger than max` errors.
remediation: On meshes near 40,000 workloads and services, raise `ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE` on istiod before upgrading (about 1MiB per 10,000 resources, e.g. `--set pilot.env.ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE=33554432`) and watch istiod logs for the error after upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods,workloadentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items | length | tostring + " pods+workloadentries"'  # near 40000 (plus services) raise ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE on istiod before the 1.31 upgrade

title: istiod's XDS API generator now rejects MCP consumers from non-system namespaces

detection.reason: which workloads consume istiod's api generator is not on the cluster

quote: Custom MCP consumers connecting to istiod's api generator from non-system namespaces are now rejected. Standard sidecar, gateway, and ztunnel traffic is unaffected.
remediation: Move custom MCP/XDS-API consumers into the Istio root namespace (or give them a control-plane identity), or set `ENABLE_XDS_API_GENERATOR_AUTH=false` on istiod. Sidecars, gateways and ztunnel need nothing.

title: istiod no longer fetches a RequestAuthentication jwksUri from link-local or cloud metadata addresses

detection.reason: RequestAuthentication objects are not collected; istiod is the subject

quote: istiod now blocks link-local and known cloud metadata addresses (such as `169.254.169.254`) at the dial level by default and rejects fetched responses that are not a valid JWKS.
remediation: A jwksUri that resolves to a link-local or cloud metadata address (169.254.0.0/16, for example) stops yielding keys after the upgrade, and requests carrying a JWT for that issuer fail validation. Serve the JWKS from another address, or inline the keys with `jwks`. A response that is not a JWKS document is now rejected at fetch time; it could not validate tokens before either.
verifyCommand: kubectl get requestauthentications.security.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.spec.jwtRules[]? | (.jwksUri // ("(inline or discovery: " + (.issuer // "?") + ")"))] | join(" "))'  # a printed URI (or discovered jwks_uri) on 169.254.0.0/16 or a cloud metadata host stops working

title: Wasm OCI images are no longer re-fetched over plain HTTP unless the registry is listed in WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES

detection.reason: WasmPlugin objects and the proxies' WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES value are not collected; istiod is the subject

quote: The plaintext retry is now only attempted for registries the operator has explicitly allowlisted via `WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES`.
remediation: A WasmPlugin whose oci:// image lives on a registry that only speaks plain HTTP no longer loads after the upgrade; with failStrategy FAIL_CLOSE (the default) its proxies then deny the traffic the plugin applies to. Serve that registry over HTTPS, or add its host to WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES on the proxies (for example through proxyMetadata) before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get wasmplugins.extensions.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + .spec.url + " failStrategy=" + (.spec.failStrategy // "FAIL_CLOSE")'  # an oci:// (or scheme-less) URL on a plain-HTTP registry needs HTTPS or a WASM_INSECURE_REGISTRIES entry

title: istiod's debug endpoints match proxyID exactly — tooling passing a partial proxy ID gets nothing back

detection.reason: which scripts or dashboards call istiod's debug endpoints is not on the cluster; istiod is the subject

quote: `proxyID` must now be the exact `<pod>.<namespace>` (or full connection ID); short forms such as `proxyID=istio-ingressgateway` no longer match.
remediation: Update scripts and dashboards that call /debug/config_dump, /debug/edsz or the istio.io/debug/config_dump XDS type with a short proxyID to pass the full `<pod>.<namespace>`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/pilot"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # callers of these istiod debug endpoints must pass the full proxyID, POD.NAMESPACE

title: A canary waypoint in another namespace is now refused for a NAMESPACE-visibility ServiceEntry, like the primary waypoint

detection.reason: serviceEntryVisibility and the waypoint's namespace are not read; Namespaces and ServiceEntries carrying the canary label (a ServiceEntry inherits its namespace's) are the population

quote: The canary waypoint is now subject to the same cross-namespace refusal as the primary.
remediation: If a ServiceEntry with NAMESPACE visibility sends its canary share through a waypoint in another namespace, that share is refused after the upgrade. Move the canary waypoint into the ServiceEntry's namespace, or drop the istio.io/use-waypoint-canary label, before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ns,serviceentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint-canary"] != null) | .kind + " " + (.metadata.namespace // "-") + "/" + .metadata.name + " canary=" + .metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint-canary"] + " canary-namespace=" + (.metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint-canary-namespace"] // "(own namespace)")'  # a canary-namespace other than the ServiceEntry's own is refused after the upgrade for a NAMESPACE-visibility ServiceEntry

title: With CRL checking on, ztunnel also refuses outbound connections and tears down open ones when a certificate is revoked

detection.reason: the CRL's contents are not collected; ztunnel DaemonSets with CRL_PATH set (the chart's peerCaCrl.enabled, off by default) are the population

quote: introduce crl enforcement for new outbound connections
remediation: Only ztunnel installed with peerCaCrl.enabled (CRL_PATH set, a plugged-in CA shipping ca-crl.pem) is affected: up to 1.30 it checked the CRL on inbound connections only; from 1.31 it also refuses outbound connections to a peer whose certificate is on the CRL, and closes connections already open when a CRL update revokes their certificate (reported as CERT_REVOKED). A client that only talked to a server with a revoked certificate stops working on upgrade — rotate those certificates first.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]?.name] | index("CRL_PATH")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'; kubectl get configmap istio-ca-crl -n istio-system -o json | jq -r '.data["ca-crl.pem"] | length | "ca-crl.pem bytes=" + tostring'  # a non-empty CRL is what gets enforced

title: In multi-network meshes ztunnel ranks other-network endpoints by locality instead of treating network as a hard tier

detection.reason: Services' traffic distribution is not joined to the mesh networks; namespaces that declare a mesh network (the multi-network marker) are the population

quote: if network is the first scope, we will prefer those that match, but will allow the remaining scopes to calculate its rank.
remediation: Only multi-network meshes with Services using locality-aware traffic distribution (PreferClose and its siblings) change: endpoints on the client's network still rank first, but endpoints on other networks are now ordered by region and zone rather than tied. Failover traffic lands closer, and on different endpoints than before — check capacity of the remote-network endpoints that now rank highest. Ambient (ztunnel) only: a mesh without a ztunnel DaemonSet can ignore this.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ns -l topology.istio.io/network -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name + " network=" + .metadata.labels["topology.istio.io/network"]'; kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.trafficDistribution != null or .metadata.annotations["networking.istio.io/traffic-distribution"] != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # these Services rank cross-network endpoints differently

title: ztunnel sizes its worker threads from its CPU limit or the node's cores instead of a flat 2

detection.reason: ZTUNNEL_WORKER_THREADS and the proxy concurrency are not read together with the CPU limit; the ztunnel DaemonSet is the subject

quote: ZTUNNEL_RESOURCE_CPU_LIMIT (set by the chart only when resources.limits.cpu is configured) is used directly as the worker-thread count.
remediation: Unless ZTUNNEL_WORKER_THREADS or proxy concurrency is set, 1.31 ztunnel runs as many worker threads as its CPU limit rounded up — one thread for a limit of 1 core or less, half the old default — and, without a limit, a quarter of the node's cores (at least 2, and at least the CPU request), so large nodes get more. A ztunnel limited to 1 CPU loses throughput on upgrade: raise the limit to 2, or set ZTUNNEL_WORKER_THREADS=2.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image | test("/ztunnel[:@]")] | any) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[] | "limits.cpu=" + (.resources.limits.cpu // "none") + " requests.cpu=" + (.resources.requests.cpu // "none") + " env=" + ([.env[]?.name] | join(","))] | join(" "))'  # a limit of 1 core or less without ZTUNNEL_WORKER_THREADS drops to one worker thread

title: OpenTelemetry tracing exports only the requests the proxy decided to sample (Envoy 1.39)

detection.reason: each proxy's sampling percentage and which Telemetry or mesh default selects the OpenTelemetry provider are not joined; the mesh ConfigMaps (istio, istio-<revision>) that define an opentelemetry extension provider are the population — a mesh whose tracing uses zipkin, datadog or another tracer is not affected

quote: Configurations that previously relied on the tracer exporting spans in those cases may export fewer OTLP spans after upgrade.
remediation: Istio 1.31 bundles Envoy 1.39, whose OpenTelemetry tracer exports a span only when the proxy's own sampling decision says so: an incoming traceparent marked sampled no longer forces it. With randomSamplingPercentage below 100 (Istio's mesh default is 1%), expect fewer spans and traces that break at the mesh where upstream SDKs sample more. Setting 100% restores parent-based export but also samples every request that arrives without a traceparent — size the collector for that, or tail-sample there.
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -n istio-system -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^istio(-[a-z0-9-]+)?$")) | .metadata.name'; kubectl get cm istio -n istio-system -o jsonpath='{.data.mesh}' | grep -n -A6 -i opentelemetry; kubectl get telemetries.telemetry.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.tracing != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " sampling=" + ([.spec.tracing[].randomSamplingPercentage // "mesh default"] | map(tostring) | join(","))'  # an opentelemetry provider sampled below 100% exports fewer spans after the upgrade
